title: New England territory bands: Mal Hallett and Joe Haymes
summary: Leeman describes famous territory bands such as Mal Hallett's and Joe Haymes's, which trained young players like Pee Wee Irwin and Johnny Mince.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Hey, and there were a lot of territory bands around at that time, that just played certain territories. Do you remember some of the names of some of those bands? That just played territories? One was New England, the New England territory. Hold this just a second while you think about it.
Tell us about some of those bands up around New England, territory bands. Did you want to get into that or did you want to wait until later?

No, no, that's all right. Previous to this, one of the famous all time territory bands was Mal Hallett, and of course, in between in the middle thirties was Joe Haymes -- he always had a great music organization; he had people with him like Pee Wee Irwin, that's how they

Sure -- and Johnny Mince on clarinet. And he used to sell bands, I think he sold a band, Tommy Dorsey's first band was one of his organized bands, and then he'd go find some more good musicians, young talent -- he was one -- Joe Haymes was the foremost.
Uh huh. I can remember him and Cab Calloway and Chick Webb talk about this Mal Hallett band because it was a territory band.
The most -- they did more one-nighters than any band ...
Yeah, but they were devastating. They had some great musicians in there.
